## Supported Action Types (23 total)

| Action | Required Params | Optional Params | Description |
|--------|----------------|-----------------|-------------|
| `agent_action` | goal | max_steps, model | Drive the game toward a natural-language goal using Claude vision (no bridge, no DOM): screenshot → Claude picks the next click/keypress → Playwright performs it → loop until done or max_steps (default 8). Sugar: `do: <goal>`. |
| `agent_assert` | check | ref, model | Verify a natural-language claim about the screen using Claude vision (no bridge): screenshot → Claude judges if `check` is true → step passes/fails. `ref` = an earlier `capture` step id for before/after claims. Sugar: `check: <claim>` (+ optional `ref:`). |
| `assert` | none | none | Pure assertion step. Requires an 'assert' block with 'bridge' and/or 'ai' sub-blocks. |
| `bo_paytable_ensure` | none | paytable_code, paytable_ref, paytable, rtp, game_id, sas_entity_id | Ensure the automation paytable exists on the master game so it is selectable per-agent (idempotent suite-setup step). |
| `bo_paytable_reset` | none | agent_id, currency_id, game_code | Reset the agent's game paytable back to the game default (teardown step; undoes bo_paytable_select). |
| `bo_paytable_select` | paytable_code | agent_id, currency_id, game_code | Point the agent's game at a named paytable so spins use it (suite-setup step). |
| `bo_paytable_update` | paytable_code | paytable_ref, paytable, game_id, sas_entity_id | Set the content of a paytable via the back-office API to force a group's determined result. |
| `bridge_action` | name | args | Call a named bridge method; the return value is stored in the step result (use 'save:' to keep it). Extra params are forwarded as method arguments. |
| `bridge_assert` | method, expected | args, path | Call a bridge method and assert its return value equals expected. Arguments may reference variables saved by earlier steps — the assertion logic lives in the game bridge (deterministic). |
| `capture` | none | none | Take a JPEG screenshot and save to the test artifact directory. |
| `click` | none | selector, x, y | Click a CSS selector or canvas coordinates. |
| `click_button` | name | require_visible | Click a named game button at its real on-screen coordinates (a genuine user tap), not by invoking its bridge action. |
| `go_offline` | none | none | Set browser context to offline mode (all network requests fail). |
| `go_online` | none | none | Restore browser context to online mode. |
| `navigate` | none | url, url_script | Navigate browser to URL. Use 'url' for static URL or 'url_script' to resolve dynamically. |
| `press_key` | key | none | Press a keyboard key (e.g., 'Space', 'Enter', 'Escape'). |
| `script` | cmd | none | Execute JavaScript in the browser context with access to previous step results and bridge. |
| `wait_for_state` | state | timeout_ms | Wait until bridge reports the given app state. |
| `wait_ms` | ms | none | Sleep for N milliseconds. ms must be > 0. |
| `wallet_balance` | none | currency | Read the player's Playsite balance via the wallet API. Stored in the step result (use 'save:' to assert it later). |
| `wallet_deposit` | amount | currency | Deposit funds into the player's wallet via the Playsite API (server-side balance change for deterministic setup). |
| `wallet_set` | amount | currency | Set the player's balance to an absolute target by depositing/withdrawing the difference (robust forcing + restore). |
| `wallet_withdraw` | amount | currency | Withdraw funds from the player's wallet via the Playsite API (server-side balance change for deterministic setup). |

### Action Notes

**`agent_action`:**
- Bridge-free, game-agnostic control: a Claude Code CLI sub-agent looks at a screenshot of the canvas and returns the next single action (click x/y, press_key, wait, done, fail); the runner performs it and re-screenshots, looping until the agent reports the goal met or 'max_steps' (default 8) is reached. 'goal' is plain English (e.g. 'open the auto-spin popup', 'increase the bet by one step') — keep goals small and observable. Uses local Claude Code auth (no API key); model via 'model:' or CLAUDE_MODEL/AGENT_MODEL (default sonnet); tunables AGENT_MAX_STEPS/AGENT_SETTLE_MS. Warm session: all do:/check: in a test share ONE persistent claude process (AGENT_STREAM=0 forces one-shot). Result is a transcript {goal, success, error, steps[]}; per-turn screenshots saved under agent/<step-id>/; every decision is appended to decisions.jsonl. Hybrid-friendly: combine with bridge_action/bridge_assert in the same test. Readable sugar: write 'do: <goal>' at the step top-level instead of action: agent_action + params.goal.

**`agent_assert`:**
- Bridge-free, vision-based verification: a Claude Code CLI sub-agent screenshots the canvas and judges whether a plain-English 'check' claim is true, returning {passed, reason, confidence}; the step passes only when passed is true. 'check' is a single observable claim (e.g. 'the spin button is visible', 'an auto-spin popup is open') — one thing per step. 'ref' is the id of an earlier 'capture' step, supplying a 'before' screenshot so claims like 'the bet is higher than before' can compare against it (resolved from the captures taken so far, robust to the screenshot counter). Uses local Claude Code auth (no API key); model via 'model:' or CLAUDE_MODEL/AGENT_MODEL (default sonnet); the verdict shows in the report. Readable sugar: write 'check: <claim>' (with optional 'ref:') at the step top-level instead of action: agent_assert.

**`assert`:**
- The 'action' field can be omitted for assert steps — if 'assert' block is present, it's inferred.

**`bo_paytable_ensure`:**
- paytable_code defaults to 'AutomationTest'. Optional paytable_ref/paytable seed the content of a newly created paytable (cloned from the game default when omitted). rtp (HIGH|MEDIUM|LOW, default MEDIUM) applies only on create. game_id/sas_entity_id default to the bo: block in games/{game}/env.config.yml. Requires BO_TOKEN/BO_REFRESH_TOKEN in .env.{suffix}.

**`bo_paytable_reset`:**
- agent_id/currency_id/game_code default to the bo: block in games/{game}/env.config.yml. Resets to the game default paytable, not the value set before the test. Requires BO_TOKEN/BO_REFRESH_TOKEN in .env.{suffix}.

**`bo_paytable_select`:**
- agent_id/currency_id/game_code default to the bo: block in games/{game}/env.config.yml. Pair with bo_paytable_reset in teardown. Requires BO_TOKEN/BO_REFRESH_TOKEN in .env.{suffix}.

**`bo_paytable_update`:**
- Provide either 'paytable_ref' (fixture stem under games/{game}/paytables/) or 'paytable' (inline dict/list/JSON string). game_id/sas_entity_id default to the bo: block in games/{game}/env.config.yml. Requires BO_TOKEN/BO_REFRESH_TOKEN in .env.{suffix}.

**`bridge_action`:**
- Two forms. (1) 'args: [..]' — ordered positional arguments calling the bridge JS method directly (window.__gameTestBridge.<name>(..)); each element is a literal except a string '$name' which resolves to a variable saved by an earlier step (use '$$' to escape a literal leading $). This is the reliable way to call methods that take an options object/array or have no Python wrapper — e.g. the Hold & Spin capture/analyser API (startEventCapture, endEventCapture, spinUntilBonus, captureHoldSpinBonus, filterBonusEvent). (2) No 'args' — any additional key-value pairs are passed as method kwargs (camelCase→snake_case), falling back to triggerAction when no wrapper exists.

**`bridge_assert`:**
- With no 'args', calls a BridgeHelper getter (e.g. isSpinEnabled). 'args: [..]' is an ordered argument list: each element is a literal, except a string '$name' which resolves to the variable saved as <name> (use '$$' to escape a literal leading $). A saved variable can appear at any position. When 'args' is given the bridge JS method is called directly, so game-exposed assert functions (e.g. testFreeSpin, verifyHoldSpinCoinsHeld) need no Python wrapper. Optional 'path' drills into a nested field of the returned value before the equality check (dot-separated; integer segments index lists) — e.g. an analyser returning {valid, bonusFound, respinCount, violations} is asserted with 'path: valid, expected: true' without pinning non-deterministic siblings.

**`click`:**
- Provide either 'selector' OR both 'x' and 'y'.

**`click_button`:**
- Resolves 'name' to a screen rect via the bridge's getButtonRect(name) (bridge-api.md §3.7), then page.mouse.click(centerX, centerY). Names: spin, stop, auto, buyBonus, nextBet, previousBet, trophy (always), plus popup element names while that popup is open (e.g. bet:row:2, auto:package:0, buyBonus:confirm). Fails if the button is absent (unknown name or its popup is closed) or — unless require_visible: false — if the rect is not visible/clickable. The resolved rect is the step result (save:-able). Pair with a wait_for_state/wait_ms afterwards if the tap opens a popup or starts a spin.

**`navigate`:**
- Provide either 'url' or 'url_script', not both.

**`script`:**
- Context provides: steps (previous results), vars (saved variables), bridge (window.__gameTestBridge), assert(cond, msg), assert_equal(a, b).

**`wait_for_state`:**
- Default `timeout_ms`: 30000

**`wallet_balance`:**
- With a 'currency' (or the configured default) the result is the numeric balance for that currency; with none it is the full list of the player's wallets. currency defaults to playsite.currency in games/{game}/env.config.{suffix}.yml (or the PLAYSITE_CURRENCY env var). Requires PLAYSITE_API_URL/PLAYSITE_USER/PLAYSITE_PASS in .env.{suffix}.

**`wallet_deposit`:**
- amount is an int/float/numeric string. currency defaults to playsite.currency in games/{game}/env.config.{suffix}.yml (or PLAYSITE_CURRENCY); a step param overrides it. Result is the updated wallet {currency, balance} (save:-able). Requires PLAYSITE_API_URL/PLAYSITE_USER/PLAYSITE_PASS in .env.{suffix}.

**`wallet_set`:**
- amount is the TARGET balance (int/float/numeric string, or a "$saved" reference to an earlier wallet_balance result). It reads the current balance and applies only the delta, so it lands on exactly amount whatever the balance was. Use it to force a precise test balance (e.g. below the bet to test a disabled spin) and — paired with a wallet_balance 'save:' in the same test's setup — to restore the original in teardown ('amount: "$orig_balance"'). currency defaults to playsite.currency / PLAYSITE_CURRENCY. Requires PLAYSITE_API_URL/PLAYSITE_USER/PLAYSITE_PASS in .env.{suffix}.

**`wallet_withdraw`:**
- amount is an int/float/numeric string. currency defaults to playsite.currency in games/{game}/env.config.{suffix}.yml (or PLAYSITE_CURRENCY); a step param overrides it. Result is the updated wallet {currency, balance} (save:-able). Fails if the balance is insufficient. Requires PLAYSITE_API_URL/PLAYSITE_USER/PLAYSITE_PASS in .env.{suffix}.

## Assert Block

An `assert` block must contain at least `bridge` or `ai` (or both).

### assert.bridge

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|-------|------|----------|-------------|
| `method` | string | Yes | Bridge getter method name |
| `expected` | any | Yes | Expected return value (equality check) |

**No other fields are supported.** Do not use `expected_type`, `expected_min_count`, etc.

### assert.ai

Supported modes: image, video

**mode: image** — required fields: `ref_screenshot`, `prompt`, `output_schema`, `expected`

**mode: video** — required fields: `video_trim`, `prompt`, `output_schema`, `expected`

**Saved-value substitution (deterministic asserts).** The `prompt` (and any
string value in `expected` / `expected_by_case`) may contain `{{name}}`
placeholders. At step-execution time each is replaced with the value an earlier
step captured via `save: name`, so the AI confirms a known value instead of
judging a fuzzy one. A `{{name}}` whose variable was never saved fails the step.
Same mechanism applies to the `check:` claim of an `agent_assert` step.

```yaml
- id: step-01
  action: bridge_action
  params: { name: getDisplayBet }
  save: bet
- id: step-02
  action: capture
- id: step-03
  assert:
    ai:
      mode: image
      ref_screenshot: step-02
      prompt: "Does the bet label show {{bet}}?"   # -> '... show 1.00?'
      output_schema: { matches: { type: boolean } }
      expected: { matches: true }
```

### Reference selection (`asset_groups` / `assets`)

Scope which manifest assets prime an AI assert instead of sending the full pack.
Settable on the `assert.ai` block AND at **test** / **group** level as an inherited
default. Precedence: **assert > test > group** — the most specific level that sets
either field wins entirely (no merge). Unset everywhere -> the full reference pack
(backward compatible). References are validated at suite load: an unknown group or
`{group}.{name}` item fails before any test runs.

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `asset_groups` | list | Manifest group names (e.g. `[symbols, ui_elements, ui]`); loads every item in each, in section order. |
| `assets` | list | Qualified `{group}.{name}` items (e.g. `[ui_elements.bet_label, symbols.coin]`); loads exactly those. |
| `ref_assets` | list | **Deprecated** alias — bare names resolved across all groups (warns). Migrate to `asset_groups`/`assets`. |

```yaml
- id: step-03
  assert:
    ai:
      mode: image
      ref_screenshot: step-02
      assets: [ui_elements.bet_label]   # only the bet label primes the model
      prompt: "Is the bet label readable and non-zero?"
      output_schema: { ok: { type: boolean } }
      expected: { ok: true }
```

## Suite File Structure

### Root-level keys

| Key | Type | Required | Description |
|-----|------|----------|-------------|
| `suite` | string | Yes | Human-readable suite title (NOT a dict) |
| `game` | string | Yes | Game identifier |
| `version` | any | Yes | Schema version |
| `config` | dict | Yes | Test configuration |
| `tests` | list | Yes* | Ungrouped test objects. *Required only if `groups` is absent — a suite needs `tests` and/or `groups`. |
| `groups` | list | Yes* | Test groups (see below). *Required only if `tests` is absent. |
| `setup` | list | No | Suite-level setup steps (run once before all groups) |
| `teardown` | list | No | Suite-level teardown steps (run once after all groups) |

### Group object (`groups[]`)

A group clusters tests that share an expensive precondition (e.g. the same
back-office paytable). Its `setup` runs **once** before the group's tests and its
`teardown` runs **once** after — not per test. Running a single test via `--test`
still runs its group's setup/teardown.

| Key | Type | Required |
|-----|------|----------|
| `id` | string | Yes (unique; used by `--group`) |
| `tests` | list | Yes (non-empty) |
| `title` | string | No |
| `setup` | list | No (runs once before the group's tests) |
| `teardown` | list | No (runs once after the group's tests) |

Test ids must be **unique across the whole suite** (so `--test <id>` is unambiguous).

### Config block

| Key | Type | Required |
|-----|------|----------|
| `test_timeout_ms` | int | Yes |
| `suite_timeout_ms` | int | Yes |
| `stop_conditions` | dict | No |
| `detection_method` | string | No |
| `video` | bool | No |

### Test object

| Key | Type | Required |
|-----|------|----------|
| `id` | string | Yes |
| `title` | string | Yes |
| `steps` | list | Yes (non-empty) |
| `setup` | list | No |
| `teardown` | list | No |
| `description` | string | No |

### Step object

| Key | Type | Required |
|-----|------|----------|
| `id` | string | Yes (always) |
| `action` | string | Yes (unless step has `assert` block) |
| `params` | dict | Depends on action |
| `assert` | dict | Required if action is `assert` or omitted |
| `description` | string | No |
| `capture` | bool | No (take screenshot after step) |
| `save` | string | No (store this step's result into `vars[<name>]` for a later `bridge_assert`) |

### Saving and asserting variables

Add `save: <name>` to any result-producing step (typically `bridge_action`)
to capture its result into a per-test variable. Assert on it later with
`bridge_assert`: its `args` list passes arguments to a bridge function, where
a string `"$name"` resolves to a saved variable (any position). The function's
return is compared to `expected`. The assertion logic lives in the game
bridge, so it is deterministic. Variables are scoped to a single test
(setup → steps → teardown).

```yaml
- id: step-05
  action: bridge_action
  params: { name: getLastPayout }
  save: payout               # vars['payout'] = result
- id: step-06
  action: bridge_assert
  params:
    method: inRange          # bridge.inRange(<payout>, 0, 100)
    args: [ "$payout", 0, 100 ]
    expected: true
```

### Capturing an event stream and asserting it with a bridge analyser

`bridge_action` with `args` calls the bridge JS method directly and keeps
its return value, so methods that take an options object/array or have no
Python wrapper (event capture, bonus analysers) are driven deterministically
— no `script`. Combine with a `bridge_assert` `path` to assert one field of an
object-returning analyser:

```yaml
- id: step-01                         # start an independent capture buffer
  action: bridge_action
  params: { name: startEventCapture, args: [ "bonus" ] }
- id: step-02                         # blocks through the whole bonus
  action: bridge_action
  params: { name: spin, args: [ 120000 ] }
- id: step-03                         # returns the captured CollectedEvent[]
  action: bridge_action
  params: { name: endEventCapture, args: [ "bonus" ] }
  save: raw
- id: step-04                         # slice the START_BONUS..END_BONUS episode
  action: bridge_action
  params: { name: filterBonusEvent, args: [ "$raw" ] }
  save: events
- id: step-05                         # analyser returns {valid, ...}; assert .valid
  action: bridge_assert
  params:
    method: verifyHoldSpinCoinsHeld   # bridge.verifyHoldSpinCoinsHeld(events).valid
    args: [ "$events" ]
    path: valid
    expected: true
```

## Runs — one execution, many test-case verdicts

A `runs:` entry (top-level, peer to `tests:`/`groups:`, or inside a group)
executes ONE procedural sequence (setup → steps → teardown) and produces a
verdict for each of several named **cases**. Use it when multiple test cases
share the same expensive execution (e.g. enter a free-spin bonus once, then
assert several things about it) instead of replaying it per case.

| Key | Type | Required | Description |
|-----|------|----------|-------------|
| `id` | string | Yes | Unique run id (unique across all test/run/case ids) |
| `title` | string | No | Human-readable run title |
| `cases` | list | Yes | Case definitions `{id, title, description?}` (≥1) |
| `setup` | list | No | Run-level setup steps |
| `steps` | list | Yes | The procedural steps (non-empty) |
| `teardown` | list | No | Run-level teardown steps |

**Tagging asserts to cases.** An assert-bearing step (an `assert` block, or
`action: bridge_assert`) carries a `case:` tag — a case id or a list of ids
(a shared analyser can feed several cases). A case's bridge verdict is the AND
of its tagged non-AI asserts. A plain (untagged) step's failure is fatal — it
means the run could not produce the data, so all cases go red.

**AI output partitioned per case (`expected_by_case`).** A single AI assert
(one trim + one model call) returns a multi-field output; `expected_by_case`
maps each case id to the subset of fields it is judged against — one call,
many case verdicts. Use `expected_by_case` instead of `expected`+`case` on the
AI block (not both). Every declared case must be covered by a `case:` tag or
an `expected_by_case` key.

Each case becomes its own verdict line in `summary.json`, all sharing the
run's single video/timeline/events (`run_id` links them). `--test <case-id>`
runs the whole run but reports that case.

```yaml
runs:
  - id: fs-3coin-countdown-run
    title: "One bonus, assert ZZ-30/32/33/35"
    cases:
      - { id: ZZ-30, title: "Trigger FS 3 coins -> 3 free spins" }
      - { id: ZZ-32, title: "Coins held fixed across re-spins" }
      - { id: ZZ-33, title: "Only non-coin cells re-spin" }
    setup: [ ... ]
    steps:
      - id: step-01                       # plain step (no case)
        action: bridge_action
        params: { name: spinUntilBonus }
      - id: step-02                       # one case
        case: ZZ-30
        assert: { bridge: { method: getFreeSpinsRemaining, expected: 3 } }
      - id: step-03                       # shared analyser -> two cases
        case: [ZZ-32, ZZ-33]
        action: bridge_assert
        params: { method: verifyHoldSpinCoinsHeld, args: ["$events"], path: valid, expected: true }
      - id: step-10                       # ONE video AI call -> per-case verdicts
        assert:
          ai:
            mode: video
            video_trim: { from_step: step-01, to_step: step-09 }
            output_schema: { coins_held: {type: boolean}, only_noncoin_cells_spin: {type: boolean}, confidence: {type: string} }
            expected_by_case:
              ZZ-32: { coins_held: true, confidence: high }
              ZZ-33: { only_noncoin_cells_spin: true, confidence: high }
    teardown: [ ... ]
```
